primaryText: A strange man lives here (and another one lives down the block). If the strange man who lives here sees a cat, he screams.
discourseSegments: A strange man lives here (and another one lives down the block).
If the strange man who lives here sees a cat, he screams.
comment: Kadmon's (1990) example as Roberts quotes it (p. 311): the descriptive content 'strange man who lives here' singles out one of the two strange men the discourse has introduced.

primaryText: A strange man lives here, and another one lives down the block. This situation makes me very nervous. If the strange man sees a cat, he screams. The other one never says anything at all.
discourseSegments: A strange man lives here, and another one lives down the block.
This situation makes me very nervous.
If the strange man sees a cat, he screams.
The other one never says anything at all.
comment: Printed with # before 'If the strange man sees a cat' (p. 312): the content 'strange man' fails to distinguish the two discourse referents, so the definite fails informational uniqueness, which familiarity alone could not explain.
